content.user_title: Review Security Pitfalls in Application Code
content.value_statement: Security mistakes often hide in key storage, caches, logs, and environment handling. This skill gives review checklists and safer patterns for those areas.
actual_capabilities: Reviews private key storage risks and safer session key patterns.
Shows frontend and backend environment variable handling guidance.
Flags unsafe logging of configuration objects and API keys.
Recommends cache time limits and avoiding sensitive cache entries.
Provides audit logging examples for sensitive operations.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not scan repositories automatically.
It does not replace a formal application security review.
Examples are TypeScript-focused and may need adaptation for other stacks.
It cannot validate runtime secret handling without project context.

use_cases.title: Review Authentication Changes
use_cases.description: Check whether session keys have expiry, permissions, and transaction limits before release.

use_cases.title: Harden Logging Practices
use_cases.description: Review application logs to avoid leaking secrets, configuration objects, or sensitive user data.

use_cases.title: Prepare Security Checklists
use_cases.description: Create practical review steps for caches, environment variables, and audit logs.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Secret Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for private key storage, secret logging, and unsafe environment variable use. List the highest priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Cache Safety Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this caching design for sensitive data exposure. Identify cache keys, stored values, expiration rules, and user-specific data risks.

prompt_templates.title: Session Key Design Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this session key design. Check permissions, expiry, per-transaction limits, encryption, and audit logging coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Release Security Gate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pre-release review across multiple files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release gate review for key storage, environment variables, logs, caches, and audit events. Return blockers, warnings, and required tests.

output_examples.input: Review logging code that prints a configuration object during startup.
output_examples.output: Finding: Do not log full configuration objects because they may contain API keys. Log only the environment name and non-sensitive status values.

output_examples.input: Review cache logic that stores a user private key under a user-specific key.
output_examples.output: Finding: Never cache private keys. Store only short-lived session tokens with strict permissions, expiration, and audit records.

output_examples.input: Review a frontend environment variable reference that uses process.env.
output_examples.output: Finding: Vite frontend variables need the VITE_ prefix. Backend-only secrets must stay on the server.

best_practices: Treat keys, tokens, connection strings, and configuration objects as sensitive by default.
Use short-lived session keys with explicit permissions, expiration, and transaction limits.
Log operational context without secrets, and add audit events for sensitive actions.
anti_patterns: Storing private keys in localStorage, plaintext databases, or shared caches.
Logging full configuration objects, API keys, or database connection strings.
Caching user-specific sensitive data without strict expiration and isolation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute security scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and examples for manual or AI-assisted code review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require access to real secrets?
faq.answer: No. Do not provide real private keys, API keys, or database credentials in prompts.

faq.question: What code areas does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on session keys, environment variables, caching, structured logging, and audit logging.

faq.question: Can it replace a security engineer?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a checklist aid, then validate critical systems with qualified security review.

faq.question: Why are unsafe examples included?
faq.answer: They are labeled anti-patterns so reviewers can recognize and remove risky code.
